```text
Issue #67 (child of head issue #12, builds on merged #65 gradient styling) started 2026-10-06. Scope: gradients stay consistent through resize/rotate/flip/duplicate, and define which elements support gradients.

- Gradient export (PNG/SVG) is issue #68 (user is speccing it in parallel), NOT #67.
- Decisions (2026-10-06): horizontal flip mirrors the gradient (reverse stops); gradient keeps rotating with the element; supported = rectangle, diamond, ellipse, triangle, iframe/embeddable, closed line/arrow/freedraw. Out of scope: text (stroke gradients not supported, too big), open lines/arrows, path, image, frame.
- Mixed selection: gradient toggle shows, applies only to supported elements. A closed line that gets opened keeps its stored gradient (hidden like solid fill; returns if re-closed).
- Gaps found in #65 code: gradient on closed line/arrow ignores negative point x; closed freedraw loses its fill; flip doesn't mirror the gradient.

**Status (2026-10-06):** branch `feat/issue-67-gradient-transformations` (from origin/master, no upstream). All 6 steps implemented and verified by the user in the browser 2026-10-06 (user committing; PR next, opened manually — no gh CLI); step 6 uses `canHaveGradient` in gradient.ts + `allowGradient` prop through ColorPicker→Picker. Decision: toggle hidden only for unfillable elements (open arrows/freedraw, 2-point lines); open lines with 3+ points keep it because applying a background auto-closes them into a polygon. With nothing selected the toggle shows. Full suite green.
- Follow-up (user-requested, 2026-10-06): gradient fill now reuses roughjs's own fill geometry (shape.ts generates a solid fill with GRADIENT_FILL_PLACEHOLDER; renderElement swaps a CanvasGradient into `options.fill`), replacing #65's hand-built paths that ignored rounded lines/freedraw curves. Step 5 revised (2026-10-06, user request): gradient swap moved from actionFlip into resizeElements.ts (resizeSingleElement `nextWidth < 0`, resizeMultipleElements `flipByX`), so Shift+H, menu flip and handle-drag flips all mirror; actionFlip is back to its pre-step-5 state. Going into the same commit as step 6, followed by an AI-logs commit.

**Why:** User manages #68 spec in parallel while working on #67.
**How to apply:** Keep #67 plans free of export work; same working style as [[hyperlink-issue-design]] (user makes design decisions, present tradeoffs).
```

```text
import { hasBackground } from "./comparisons";
import { canBecomePolygon } from "./typeChecks";
import { isPathALoop } from "./utils";

import type { ExcalidrawElement } from "./types";

export type GradientType = "linear" | "radial";

/**
 * Solid fill used when generating rough shapes for gradient backgrounds, so
 * roughjs builds its normal fill geometry. The canvas renderer swaps it for
 * the actual CanvasGradient at draw time. Invisible, but not the literal
 * "transparent", which roughjs' path() treats as "no fill".
 */
export const GRADIENT_FILL_PLACEHOLDER = "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)";

export type GradientColors = Readonly<{
  type: GradientType;
  startColor: string;
  endColor: string;
}>;

export const getGradientColors = (
  backgroundColor: string,
): GradientColors | null => {
  const isLinear = backgroundColor.startsWith("linear-gradient(90deg,");
  const isRadial = backgroundColor.startsWith("radial-gradient(circle,");
  if ((!isLinear && !isRadial) || !backgroundColor.endsWith(")")) {
    return null;
  }

  const prefix = isLinear
    ? "linear-gradient(90deg,"
    : "radial-gradient(circle,";
  const stops = backgroundColor.slice(prefix.length, -1);
  let parentheses = 0;
  for (let index = 0; index < stops.length; index++) {
    if (stops[index] === "(") {
      parentheses++;
    } else if (stops[index] === ")") {
      parentheses--;
    } else if (stops[index] === "," && parentheses === 0) {
      const startColor = stops.slice(0, index).trim();
      const endColor = stops.slice(index + 1).trim();
      return startColor && endColor
        ? { type: isLinear ? "linear" : "radial", startColor, endColor }
        : null;
    }
  }
  return null;
};

/**
 * Whether a gradient background can ever be visible on the element.
 * Lines, arrows and freedraw only fill when closed; open lines with 3+
 * points still qualify because applying a background closes them into a
 * polygon (see actionChangeBackgroundColor).
 */
export const canHaveGradient = (element: ExcalidrawElement) => {
  if (!hasBackground(element.type)) {
    return false;
  }
  switch (element.type) {
    case "line":
      return isPathALoop(element.points) || canBecomePolygon(element.points);
    case "arrow":
    case "freedraw":
      return isPathALoop(element.points);
    default:
      return true;
  }
};

/**
 * Mirrors a linear gradient for a horizontal flip by swapping its stops.
 * Radial gradients and solid colors are symmetric, so they're returned as-is.
 */
export const flipGradientHorizontally = (backgroundColor: string) => {
  const gradientColors = getGradientColors(backgroundColor);
  return gradientColors?.type === "linear"
    ? createGradientBackground(
        "linear",
        gradientColors.endColor,
        gradientColors.startColor,
      )
    : backgroundColor;
};

export const createGradientBackground = (
  type: GradientType,
  startColor: string,
  endColor: string,
) =>
  type === "linear"
    ? `linear-gradient(90deg, ${startColor}, ${endColor})`
    : `radial-gradient(circle, ${startColor}, ${endColor})`;
  );
};

const drawElementOnCanvas = (
  element: NonDeletedExcalidrawElement,
  rc: RoughCanvas,
  context: CanvasRenderingContext2D,
  renderConfig: StaticCanvasRenderConfig,
) => {
  /**
   * Builds the CanvasGradient for a gradient background, or null when the
   * element has none (or can't be filled, e.g. an open line).
   */
  const createGradientFill = () => {
    const gradientColors = getGradientColors(element.backgroundColor);
    if (!gradientColors) {
      return null;
    }

    // box the gradient spans, in element-local coordinates
    let [x1, y1, x2, y2] = [0, 0, element.width, element.height];
    if (
      element.type === "line" ||
      element.type === "arrow" ||
      element.type === "freedraw"
    ) {
      if (!isPathALoop(element.points) || !element.points.length) {
        return null;
      }
      // points can extend left of / above the element origin
      [x1, y1, x2, y2] = getBoundsFromPoints(element.points);
    }

    const centerX = (x1 + x2) / 2;
    const centerY = (y1 + y2) / 2;
    const gradient =
      gradientColors.type === "linear"
        ? context.createLinearGradient(x1, y1, x2, y1)
        : context.createRadialGradient(
            centerX,
            centerY,
            0,
            centerX,
            centerY,
            Math.hypot((x2 - x1) / 2, (y2 - y1) / 2),
          );
    gradient.addColorStop(
      0,
      applyDarkModeFilter(
        gradientColors.startColor,
        renderConfig.theme === THEME.DARK,
      ),
    );
    gradient.addColorStop(
      1,
      applyDarkModeFilter(
        gradientColors.endColor,
        renderConfig.theme === THEME.DARK,
      ),
    );
    return gradient;
  };

  /**
   * Gradient shapes are generated with a placeholder solid fill (see
   * generateRoughOptions), so roughjs draws its regular fill geometry; here
   * we hand it the gradient instead. Copies the shape so the cache is
   * untouched.
   */
  const withGradientFill = (
    shape: Drawable,
    gradient: CanvasGradient | null,
  ): Drawable =>
    gradient
      ? {
          ...shape,
          options: {
            ...shape.options,
            // roughjs assigns `fill` straight to ctx.fillStyle
            fill: gradient as unknown as string,
          },
        }
      : shape;

  switch (element.type) {
    case "rectangle":
    case "iframe":
    case "embeddable":
    case "diamond":
    case "triangle":
    case "ellipse": {
      context.lineJoin = "round";
      context.lineCap = "round";

      rc.draw(
        withGradientFill(
          ShapeCache.generateElementShape(element, renderConfig),
          createGradientFill(),
        ),
      );
      break;
    }
    case "arrow":
    case "line": {
      context.lineJoin = "round";
      context.lineCap = "round";

      const gradient = createGradientFill();
      ShapeCache.generateElementShape(element, renderConfig).forEach(
        (shape, index) => {
          // the line/curve (with its fill) is always first; the rest are
          // arrowheads, which keep their own fills
          rc.draw(index === 0 ? withGradientFill(shape, gradient) : shape);
        },
      );
      break;
    }
    case "path": {
      // schematic, not hand-drawn — plain dashed polyline + waypoint dots,
      // drawn directly (no roughjs sketch, see generateElementShape())
      context.save();
      context.lineJoin = "round";
      context.lineCap = "round";
      context.strokeStyle = applyDarkModeFilter(
        element.strokeColor,
        renderConfig.theme === THEME.DARK,
      );
      context.fillStyle = context.strokeStyle;
      context.lineWidth = element.strokeWidth;

      if (element.points.length > 1) {
        context.setLineDash([element.strokeWidth * 3, element.strokeWidth * 2]);
        context.beginPath();
        element.points.forEach(([x, y], index) => {
          if (index === 0) {
            context.moveTo(x, y);
          } else {
            context.lineTo(x, y);
          }
        });
        context.stroke();
        context.setLineDash([]);
      }

      const dotRadius = Math.max(element.strokeWidth * 1.5, 3);
      element.points.forEach(([x, y]) => {
        context.beginPath();
        context.arc(x, y, dotRadius, 0, Math.PI * 2);
        context.fill();
      });

      context.restore();
      break;
    }
    case "freedraw": {
      // Draw directly to canvas
      context.save();

      const gradient = createGradientFill();
      const shapes = ShapeCache.generateElementShape(element, renderConfig);

      for (const shape of shapes) {
        if (typeof shape === "string") {
          context.fillStyle = applyDarkModeFilter(
            element.strokeColor,
            renderConfig.theme === THEME.DARK,
          );
          context.fill(new Path2D(shape));
        } else {
          rc.draw(withGradientFill(shape, gradient));
        }
      }

      context.restore();
      break;
    }
    case "image": {
      context.save();
      const cacheEntry =
        element.fileId !== null
          ? renderConfig.imageCache.get(element.fileId)
    stroke: applyDarkModeFilter(element.strokeColor, isDarkMode),
    preserveVertices:
      continuousPath || element.roughness < ROUGHNESS.cartoonist,
  };

  switch (element.type) {
    case "rectangle":
    case "iframe":
    case "embeddable":
    case "diamond":
    case "triangle":
    case "ellipse": {
      if (getGradientColors(element.backgroundColor)) {
        options.fillStyle = "solid";
        options.fill = GRADIENT_FILL_PLACEHOLDER;
      } else {

          ? undefined

      if (element.type === "ellipse") {

      }
      return options;

    case "arrow":

          options.fill = GRADIENT_FILL_PLACEHOLDER;
```

```text
const renderElementToSvg = (
  element: Readonly<NonDeletedExcalidrawElement>,
  elementsMap: RenderableElementsMap,
  rsvg: RoughSVG,
  svgRoot: SVGElement,
  files: BinaryFiles,
  offsetX: number,
  offsetY: number,
  renderConfig: SVGRenderConfig,
) => {
  const offset = { x: offsetX, y: offsetY };
  const [x1, y1, x2, y2] = getElementAbsoluteCoords(element, elementsMap);
  let cx = (x2 - x1) / 2 - (element.x - x1);

        container,
        element as ExcalidrawTextElementWithContainer,
        elementsMap,

      cx = (x2 - x1) / 2 - (boundTextCoords.x - x1);
      cy = (y2 - y1) / 2 - (boundTextCoords.y - y1);
      offsetX = offsetX + boundTextCoords.x - element.x;
      offsetY = offsetY + boundTextCoords.y - element.y;

  let root = svgRoot;

    anchorTag.setAttribute("href", normalizeLink(element.link));
    root.appendChild(anchorTag);
```

Here's my draft for issue #68 (gradient export). I couldn't open the issue text because `gh` isn't installed, so this is built from my notes (#68 covers PNG/SVG export) and the current code. Tell me if the issue's scope is different.

## Where things stand

- **PNG** export goes through the same canvas `renderElement` path, so gradients probably export correctly already. That still needs checking, not assuming.
- **SVG** export loses gradients. [staticSvgScene.ts](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticSvgScene.ts) draws the cached rough shape, whose fill is `GRADIENT_FILL_PLACEHOLDER` (`rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`), so gradient fills come out transparent.
- **Embedded scene data** is fine. `backgroundColor` round-trips untouched through [restore.ts:446](packages/excalidraw/data/restore.ts#L446).

## Draft steps

1. **Pull the gradient geometry into one shared helper.** Move the box and center/radius math out of `createGradientFill` in [renderElement.ts:343](packages/element/src/renderElement.ts#L343) into a `getGradientGeometry(element)` in [gradient.ts](packages/element/src/gradient.ts). It would return the type, the colors and the local coordinates, or null for unfillable or open shapes. Canvas keeps working the same way, and SVG then uses the exact same numbers, so the two outputs can't drift apart.

2. **Write gradients into SVG `<defs>`.** Add a `<linearGradient>` or `<radialGradient>` with `id="gradient-<elementId>"` and `gradientUnits="userSpaceOnUse"`, using element-local coordinates. The node's existing `translate/rotate` transform then carries rotation along, matching #67's rule that the gradient rotates with the element. Stop colors go through `applyDarkModeFilter` when `exportWithDarkMode` is on.

3. **Point the fill path at the gradient.** In each SVG case (rectangle/diamond/triangle/ellipse, iframe/embeddable, closed line/arrow with only the first shape and not the arrowheads, closed freedraw), find the rough fill path and set `fill="url(#gradient-<id>)"`. Element and frame opacity keep working through the existing `fill-opacity`.

4. **Check PNG and clipboard.** Confirm PNG export and "copy as PNG/SVG" in both light and dark export. Also check the export dialog preview, since it renders through the same path.

5. **Tests.** Add SVG snapshot and DOM assertions to [packages/excalidraw/tests/gradient.test.tsx](packages/excalidraw/tests/gradient.test.tsx): `<defs>` has the right gradient, the fill references it, rotated and flipped elements are correct, dark mode is filtered, an open line gets no gradient, and two gradient elements get unique ids. Add a unit test for `getGradientGeometry`.

## Decisions for you

- **Finding the fill path in step 3.** One option is to match the node whose `fill` equals the placeholder: simple, but it depends on how roughjs writes its output. The other is to draw the fill drawable separately. My recommendation is the placeholder match, kept behind a small helper.
- **SVG gradient ids.** `gradient-<elementId>` is deterministic and good for snapshots. A collision is only possible if someone inlines two exported SVGs of the same scene on one page. A per-export random suffix would avoid that but makes snapshots noisy.
- **Out of scope?** Library item thumbnails also use SVG export, so step 3 fixes them for free. Explicitly excluding them, or just verifying them, is your call.

Do you want me to start on step 1, or change the scope first?

```bash
      x1: 0,
      y1: 0,
      x2: 200,
    });
  });

      type: "radial",
      cx: 100,
      cy: 50,
      r: Math.hypot(100, 50),
    });

      x2: 60,
      cx: 5,
      cy: 10,
    });
  });
```

I've made the `feat/issue-68-gradient-export` branch off the #67 branch and finished step 1: the canvas renderer now gets its gradient numbers from one shared helper that the SVG export will use too. The typecheck passes, the existing canvas gradient tests in [gradient.test.tsx](packages/excalidraw/tests/gradient.test.tsx) still pass, and all 64 gradient tests are green.

- **New helper:** `getGradientGeometry(element)` in [gradient.ts](packages/element/src/gradient.ts) holds the math that used to sit inside the canvas renderer. It returns the gradient type, its two colors and its position in the element's own coordinates, or `null` when there's no gradient or the shape can't be filled (like an open line). It leaves dark mode to the caller.
- **Canvas renderer:** `createGradientFill` in [renderElement.ts](packages/element/src/renderElement.ts) now just calls the helper. I removed two imports it no longer needs.
- **Tests:** I added 4 tests in [packages/element/src/**tests**/gradient.test.ts](packages/element/src/__tests__/gradient.test.ts). They cover a straight gradient across the box, a round gradient's center and size, a closed line with points left of and above its origin, and `null` for open lines and solid colors.

Nothing should look different on screen. A quick check in the browser that gradients look the same as before (including a closed line drawn up and to the left) would confirm it. Once you're happy, I'll start step 2, which writes the gradients into the SVG export.

```text
const roughSVGDrawWithPrecision = (
  rsvg: RoughSVG,
  drawable: Drawable,
  precision?: number,
) => {
  if (typeof precision === "undefined") {
    return rsvg.draw(drawable);
  }
  const pshape: Drawable = {
    sets: drawable.sets,
    shape: drawable.shape,
    options: { ...drawable.options, fixedDecimalPlaceDigits: precision },
  };
  return rsvg.draw(pshape);
};

const maybeWrapNodesInFrameClipPath = (
  element: Readonly<NonDeletedExcalidrawElement>,
  root: SVGElement,
  nodes: SVGElement[],
  frameRendering: AppState["frameRendering"],
  elementsMap: RenderableElementsMap,
) => {
  if (!frameRendering.enabled || !frameRendering.clip) {
    return null;
  }
  const frame = getContainingFrame(element, elementsMap);
  if (frame) {
    const g = root.ownerDocument.createElementNS(SVG_NS, "g");
    g.setAttributeNS(SVG_NS, "clip-path", `url(#${frame.id})`);
    nodes.forEach((node) => g.appendChild(node));
    return g;
  }

  return null;
};
```

```bash
s=s.replace('''const maybeWrapNodesInFrameClipPath = (''','''/**
 * Adds the element's gradient background to the SVG's <defs>, in
 * element-local coordinates so the element node's own translate/rotate
 * places it (same geometry as the canvas renderer). Returns the fill
 * reference, or null when the element has no visible gradient.
 */
const addGradientDef = (
  element: Readonly<NonDeletedExcalidrawElement>,
  svgRoot: SVGElement,
  renderConfig: SVGRenderConfig,
): string | null => {
  const geometry = canHaveGradient(element)
    ? getGradientGeometry(element)
    : null;
  if (!geometry) {
    return null;
  }

  const id = `gradient-${element.id}`;
  const gradient = svgRoot.ownerDocument.createElementNS(
    SVG_NS,
    geometry.type === "linear" ? "linearGradient" : "radialGradient",
  );
  gradient.setAttribute("id", id);
  gradient.setAttribute("gradientUnits", "userSpaceOnUse");
  if (geometry.type === "linear") {
    gradient.setAttribute("x1", `${geometry.x1}`);
    gradient.setAttribute("y1", `${geometry.y1}`);
    gradient.setAttribute("x2", `${geometry.x2}`);
    gradient.setAttribute("y2", `${geometry.y1}`);
  } else {
    gradient.setAttribute("cx", `${geometry.cx}`);
    gradient.setAttribute("cy", `${geometry.cy}`);
    gradient.setAttribute("r", `${geometry.r}`);
  }

  [geometry.startColor, geometry.endColor].forEach((color, index) => {
    const stop = svgRoot.ownerDocument.createElementNS(SVG_NS, "stop");
    stop.setAttribute("offset", `${index}`);
    stop.setAttribute(
      "stop-color",
      applyDarkModeFilter(color, renderConfig.theme === THEME.DARK),
    );
    gradient.appendChild(stop);
  });

  (svgRoot.querySelector("defs") || svgRoot).appendChild(gradient);
  return `url(#${id})`;
};
```

Step 2 is done. SVG export now writes each gradient into the file's `<defs>` section, but shapes don't use it yet, so their fill still comes out transparent until step 3. Typecheck, eslint and the full suite (117 files, run with `--maxWorkers=4`) all pass, and no snapshots changed.

**What changed:**

- I added `addGradientDef` to [staticSvgScene.ts](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticSvgScene.ts), and `renderElementToSvg` calls it for every element.
- For each element that can show a gradient, it adds a `<linearGradient>` or `<radialGradient>` named `gradient-<elementId>` to `<defs>`. It uses the same numbers as the canvas, via the step 1 helper, and in the element's own coordinates, so the element's existing translate/rotate places it.
- In dark-mode export, the colors get the same dark-mode filter as the canvas.
- Open lines, solid fills and elements that can't take gradients get nothing.
- Above that call there's a `TODO(#68 step 3)` comment, which step 3 will replace.

**Tests:** I added 6 SVG export tests to [packages/excalidraw/tests/gradient.test.tsx](packages/excalidraw/tests/gradient.test.tsx):

- a straight gradient spanning the element
- a round gradient's center and size
- a closed line with points left of and above its origin
- dark-mode colors
- separate ids for two gradient elements
- nothing added for an open line or a solid fill

**To check in the browser:** export a gradient rectangle as SVG and open the file in a text editor. You should see a `<linearGradient id="gradient-…">` inside `<defs>`, and the shape should still look empty when opened in a browser. That's expected until step 3.

Step 3 is done: exported SVGs now fill each shape with its gradient. The full suite passes (117 files), typecheck and eslint are clean, and no snapshots changed.

**What changed in [staticSvgScene.ts](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticSvgScene.ts):**

- `renderElementToSvg` keeps the gradient reference that `addGradientDef` returns, and the step 2 TODO is gone.
- When an element is added to the SVG, a new `applyGradientFill` finds that element's placeholder fill and replaces it with `url(#gradient-<id>)`. It only looks inside that element's own nodes.
- Arrowheads never use the placeholder, so they keep their own fill.
- Every element type goes through this same step, so links, frame clipping and opacity work without any per-type changes.

**Tests:** I added 9 more to [packages/excalidraw/tests/gradient.test.tsx](packages/excalidraw/tests/gradient.test.tsx), which now has 51:

- rectangle, diamond, ellipse, embeddable, closed line and closed freedraw each get the gradient fill, and no placeholder fill is left anywhere
- a closed arrow gets the gradient while its arrowhead keeps the red stroke color
- an element with a link still gets the gradient inside its `<a>`
- 50% opacity still applies to the gradient fill

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-07 06:58:19Z)**_

Yes, that's intended. Dark mode inverts every color, gradients included:

- **Solid fills and strokes:** a black rectangle or a black stroke also turns light in a dark-mode export. Excalidraw's dark mode works by inverting all colors.
- **How it inverts:** it's [`applyDarkModeFilter`](packages/common/src/colors.ts#L83), which inverts each color by 93% and then rotates the hue 180°. Black becomes a near-white `#ededed` (not pure white), white becomes near-black, and colored stops stay roughly the same hue, so a red stays reddish.
- **Canvas:** the dark-mode canvas already showed your gradients this way during #67, because `createGradientFill` uses the same filter.

So the SVG matches the canvas.

To compare, put a solid black rectangle next to the gradient and export with dark mode on. Both should turn light the same way. If they don't, that's a bug and I'll look into it.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-07 07:07:46Z)**_

Step 4 is done. No new code was needed: every export path already gets gradients right, and the tests now cover the parts that could break. Typecheck, eslint and the gradient tests pass (54). The full suite also passed (117 files); since then I've changed only types in one test.

**Where each export path goes:**

| Path | Function | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Export PNG, copy as PNG | `exportToCanvas` | correct already (same canvas drawing as the editor); now tested |
| Export dialog preview | `exportToCanvas` (via utils) | same as PNG |
| Export SVG, copy as SVG | `exportToSvg` | fixed in steps 2–3 |
| Library thumbnails | `exportToSvg` (via utils, restores elements first) | gradient survives the restore; now tested |

**Tests:** I added 3 to [packages/excalidraw/tests/gradient.test.tsx](packages/excalidraw/tests/gradient.test.tsx):

- PNG export of a rotated, offset rectangle builds the gradient as `(0, 0, 200, 0)` in the element's own coordinates and paints one gradient fill
- dark-mode PNG export passes the gradient colors through the dark-mode filter
- a library thumbnail, exported with the same call `useLibraryItemSvg` makes, contains the `<radialGradient>` and the fill points at it

**Things I fixed in my own work:**

- One assertion was written as `.not.toBeNull` without the `()`, so it never actually checked anything. It's fixed.
- My Python edits had written Windows line endings into the test file. I converted them back, and none of the changed files have them now.
- The typecheck caught missing layout fields on the test's app state. I added them.

**Library thumbnails only take colors from the source code.** [useLibraryItemSvg.ts](packages/excalidraw/hooks/useLibraryItemSvg.ts) always exports thumbnails in light mode and has an existing TODO noting that dark mode uses a CSS filter. Dark-mode thumbnails therefore get a CSS invert, not our color filter, the same as every other color in a thumbnail. That's how the app already works, so I've left it alone.

**To check in the browser:**

- PNG export with dark mode on and off
- copy as PNG and paste into another app
- copy as SVG and paste into a text editor
- the export dialog preview
- adding a gradient shape to the library and looking at its thumbnail

The library is a sidebar that opens from the **Library** button (book icon) in the top-right corner of the editor, next to Share.

To check a gradient thumbnail:

1. Select a shape that has a gradient fill.
2. Right-click it and choose **Add to library**.
3. Open the **Library** sidebar. The new item's thumbnail should show the gradient.

Also switch the editor to dark mode with the library open. The thumbnail should invert like the rest of the library items, because thumbnails use the CSS filter I mentioned.

Step 5 is done, and that finishes the plan for #68. The final pass turned up one small improvement and added tests for frames. Typecheck, eslint and the full suite (117 files) pass, and no snapshots changed.

**What I checked:**

- **Frames, clipped:** a gradient element inside a clipped frame still gets its gradient fill inside the clip group. This is now tested.
- **Exporting a single frame:** the child's gradient is still defined and used when you export just that frame. This is now tested.
- **Embeddables rendered live:** fine, as described above. The gradient goes on the placeholder rectangle only, and the live iframe node has no leftover fill.
- **Embeddable label text:** text can't take a gradient, so it doesn't get one.

**One change in [staticSvgScene.ts](packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticSvgScene.ts):** gradient coordinates are now rounded to 2 decimals (`MAX_DECIMALS_FOR_SVG_EXPORT`), the same as the shape outlines. A radial `r` was coming out as `111.80339887498948` and is now `111.8`. That makes the SVG smaller and easier to read, and looks the same.

**Tests:** 56 in [packages/excalidraw/tests/gradient.test.tsx](packages/excalidraw/tests/gradient.test.tsx), including the 2 new frame tests. The radial test now expects the rounded `111.8`.

**To check in the browser:** put a gradient shape partly outside a frame and export. The overhang should be clipped, and the visible part should still show the gradient. Also try exporting just the frame.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-07 07:42:25Z)**_

Written for: the reviewers on the PR.

The things reviewers should know:

1. **The base branch is #67.** The PR targets `feat/issue-67-gradient-transformations` because #67 is waiting on a second reviewer. It needs a retarget to `master` after #67 merges.
2. **PNG export needed no code change.** It already used the editor's canvas drawing. This PR only adds tests for it.
3. **SVG matches the canvas because both use one shared helper.** `getGradientGeometry` holds the math, so the two can't drift apart.
4. **How the SVG fill is found.** Gradient shapes are drawn with a placeholder fill, and the SVG step swaps that placeholder for the gradient. Arrowheads never use the placeholder, so they're left alone.
5. **Gradient ids** are deterministic, `gradient-<elementId>`. Two exported SVGs of the same scene placed on one web page could clash, which is unlikely, and the stable ids keep snapshots readable.
6. **Library thumbnails in dark mode** use a CSS invert, which was already the case for all thumbnail colors (there's a TODO in `useLibraryItemSvg`). Out of scope here.
7. **Snapshots and test runs.** No snapshot changes. On Windows, run the full suite with `--maxWorkers=4`, because plain `test:update` times out unrelated tests and deletes their snapshots.

A description you can paste:

```markdown
## Summary

Closes #68. Gradient backgrounds now survive export.

- **SVG export:** gradients are written to `<defs>` as `linearGradient`/`radialGradient` (`userSpaceOnUse`, element-local coords) and the shape's fill points at them. Rotation, flips, opacity, links, frame clipping and dark-mode export all carry over.
- **PNG export / copy as PNG / export preview:** already correct (same canvas path as the editor); now covered by tests.
- **Library thumbnails:** get the SVG fix automatically; verified.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Based on #67** (not yet merged). Will retarget to `master` once #67 lands.
- Canvas and SVG share one geometry helper, `getGradientGeometry` (`packages/element/src/gradient.ts`), so they can't drift.
- The SVG renderer finds the fill by its placeholder color (`GRADIENT_FILL_PLACEHOLDER`) and swaps in `url(#gradient-<elementId>)`. Arrowheads are untouched.
- Gradient coords are rounded to `MAX_DECIMALS_FOR_SVG_EXPORT`, like the rough paths.
- Out of scope: library thumbnails in dark mode still use the existing CSS invert (see TODO in `useLibraryItemSvg.ts`).

## Testing

- New tests in `packages/element/src/__tests__/gradient.test.ts` and `packages/excalidraw/tests/gradient.test.tsx` (`yarn vitest run gradient`)
- Full suite, typecheck, eslint and prettier pass; no snapshot changes
- Manually verified: SVG/PNG export (light + dark), copy as PNG/SVG, export preview, library thumbnails, frames

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
```
